schemes.english_name: Brunel Business School Co-Innovate collaborative student projects with SMEs
schemes.description: Local SMEs/start-ups write project briefs (social media, marketing, new product launch, HR, accounting/finance); students apply with a CV and statement, are matched, sign a three-party contract (student, business, university) and work on campus on the brief with weekly student and monthly supervisor meetings, ending in a final report. Can be used as a final-year project or dissertation.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Brunel Business School students; wider cross-university eligibility not evidenced
schemes.credit_assessment: Final-year project/dissertation route (30 credits per BSc BME page); otherwise not stated
schemes.duration: 3 weeks to 3/5 months, or across the academic year (sources differ)
schemes.delivery_format: On campus, supervised by academic tutor
schemes.project_evidence: Business-written brief with scope/objectives and a final report (src 1).
schemes.group_evidence: Source says projects can be undertaken 'either as an individual or in a small team'; routes not separable (src 1).
schemes.employer_evidence: SME writes the brief, is party to a tri-partite contract, and IP terms are agreed with the company (src 1).
schemes.partner_role: Client SME supplies live brief and IP agreement.
schemes.unresolved: Page undated; fetched page does not mention funding or credits (ERDF reference from earlier search summary not confirmed). Team vs individual not separable; no dated 2025/26 source, so current delivery unverified.

profile_md: Brunel's clearest employer-linked route is Brunel Business School's Co-Innovate: SMEs write a project brief, a contract is issued on matching, work runs over the academic year and ends in a final report; it can be the 30-credit final-year project (BSc Business Management with Entrepreneurship). The page states projects can be done "either as an individual or in a small team", so group working is Unclear, the pages are undated, and 2025/26 delivery is unverified. Other leads: Design+ (businesses work with students on Final Year Projects since 2004; Brompton Bikes, Hornby, BT, JLR named; group/individual not stated), Leadership for Change (Year 3, students with a community organisation; compulsory/optional status inconsistent), MSc Project Management live consultancy (no clients named), Global Challenges BASc 8-week placement or group project (page not retrievable) and the Feb 2025 Enterprise Mobility Challenge (detail truncated). Engineering, computing, science and law searches found group projects without external clients. No route is verified as meeting all three criteria with current delivery; provision is distributed and programme-level.
gaps: No dated 2025/26 evidence for any route; Co-Innovate team vs individual not separable; Design+ group status unknown; Global Challenges and Enterprise Mobility Challenge pages truncated; MSc PM client detail missing; further departmental capstones likely; reduced-depth search.
